## 🔧 “new row violates row‑level security policy” – the quick fix for your Bolt + Supabase app The error means Supabase is checking its **Row‑Level Security (RLS)** rules before allowing a new row to be written. By default RLS is turned **off** for new tables, but Bolt makes it **on** automatically for any table you create so that users can’t see each‑other’s data. The policy that allows inserts is missing (or only allows inserts for a certain role that your app isn’t using). Below is a *single‑step, safe* way to add the policy. All changes are **server‑side** (no secrets exposed) and will NOT let anyone else read your data. > **⚠️ What we are doing** > *Add an “insert” policy that lets the authenticated user add rows to your table.* > **⚙️ What you’ll need** > • Supabase dashboard (or CLI) > • The name of the table that is failing > • The role your app is using (`authenticated` is the most common) If you’re unsure which table it is, the browser console will show you – it looks like `mytable` or `notes`. --- ### Step 1 – Open the Supabase dashboard 1. Log into **supabase.io** → your project. 2. In the left‑hand menu click **Database → Tables**. 3. Click the table that the error mentioned (e.g. `notes`).
🦾 **Tip:** If you’re not sure, look in the console of your app (the error message will include the table name). --- ### Step 2 – Enable RLS (if it isn’t already) 1. On the table page, under **Table Settings** → **Row Level Security**, toggle **ON**.
✅ *Leave the switch ON – it protects your data.* --- ### Step 3 – Add an “insert” policy 1. Still on the same table page, click **Policies** → **New Policy**. 2. Fill in the form: | Field | Value | Why | |-------|-------|-----| | **Name** | `allow-insert` | Any name, but something descriptive is nice | | **Role** | `authenticated` | Users who are logged in. If your app uses a different role, pick that one. | | **Using** | `true` | Allow the action if the condition is true. | | **Expression** | `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL` | Ensures only logged‑in users can add a row. | | **Check** | *Leave blank (or `true`)* | No extra check needed for inserts. | 3. Click **Save Policy**. > 🎉 You’ve just told Supabase: *“If a user is logged in, let them add a row.”* > This matches the typical Bolt + Supabase flow and fixes the “violates RLS policy” error. --- ### Step 4 – Test the change 1. Go back to your Bolt app. 2. Try creating the row again (e.g. adding a new note or item). • If it still shows an error, refresh the browser to clear any cached policies. • If it works, you’ll see your new row appear in the table. --- ### Step 5 – (Optional) tighten the policy further If you want to limit *which* data a user can write (e.g. only set their own `user_id`), modify the **Expression**: ```sql auth.uid() = ``` Replace `` with the name of the column that stores the user’s ID (often `user_id`). --- #### Quick FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | **Can I delete this policy later?** | Yes – click the policy and choose “Delete”. | | **Will it expose my data to other users?** | No – policy only affects inserts, not selects. | | **Do I need a separate policy for updates/deletes?** | Only if you want users to edit or remove their rows. | --- ### Save Point In Bolt, the dashboard itself acts as a save point. If something goes wrong, just **refresh the dashboard** or **undo** the policy in the “Policies” tab. There's no hidden code to risk. --- **All set!** 🎉 You’ve restored the ability to add rows without compromising your privacy. If you run into any other errors or run into a different table, just let me know the table name and the exact message – I’ll guide you through the next policy in the same way.
